questions.q:
By interchanging the given two signs and numbers which of the following equation will be not correct?

+ and ×, 5 and 4

I. 4 + 8 × 5 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37

II. 5 × 3 – 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = –8
questions.solution:
I. 4 + 8 × 5 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37

After interchanging the signs + and ×, and numbers, 5 and 4 in the given equation, we have

5 × 8 + 4 – 7 ÷ 1 = 37

Applying BODMAS Rule, we get

5 × 8 + 4 – 7 = 37

⇒ 40 + 4 – 7 = 37

⇒ 44 - 7 = 37

⇒ 37 = 37

The given equation is correct.

II. 5 × 3 – 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = –8

After interchanging the signs + and ×, and numbers, 5 and 4 in the given equation, we have

4 + 3 – 5 × 6 ÷ 2 = –8

Applying BODMAS Rule, we get

4 + 3 – 5 × 3 = –8

⇒ 4 + 3 – 15 = –8

⇒ 7 – 15 = –8

⇒ -8 = –8

The given equation is correct.

Hence, "Neither I nor II" is the correct answer.

• Each carbon atom generates three sigma bonds with three other carbon atoms in the fullerene's sp2 hybridization state.

Additional Information

• HIV proteases' hydrophobic cavity can accommodate fullerene, which prevents substrates from reaching the enzyme's catalytic site. It has antioxidant and radical scavenger properties. Fullerene can also produce significant quantum yields of singlet oxygen when exposed to light.

questions.q: What is the present value of Rs.10,000 received in 2 years, if the interest rate is 12% per year, compounded semi-annually?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Effective interest rate per period = 12% ÷ 2 = 6% = 0.06

Total compounding periods (n) = 2 years × 2 = 4 periods

Present Value (PV) = FV ÷ (1 + r)ⁿ = 10,000 ÷ (1.06)⁴

Using (1.06)⁴ ≈ 1.262477

PV = 10,000 ÷ 1.262477 ≈ ₹7,920.94

Alternate Method

Future Value (FV) = ₹10,000

Annual Interest Rate (R) = 12%

Time (T) = 2 years

Compounding = Semi-annually (m = 2)

Formula Used:

Present Value (PV) = FV ÷ [1 + (R ÷ m)]m × T

•

PV = ?
FV = ₹10,000
Start (T=0)
End (T=2 yrs)

4 periods of 6% each
PV = 10,000 ÷ (1.06)⁴

Calculations:

⇒ Semi-annual rate (r) = 12% ÷ 2 = 6% = 0.06

⇒ Number of periods (n) = 2 × 2 = 4

⇒ PV = 10,000 ÷ (1 + 0.06)⁴

⇒ PV = 10,000 ÷ (1.06)⁴

⇒ PV = 10,000 ÷ (1.06 × 1.06 × 1.06 × 1.06)

⇒ PV = 10,000 ÷ 1.26247696

⇒ PV = 7920.9365...

⇒ PV ≈ ₹7,920.94

∴ The correct answer is ₹7,920.94.

Additional Information

Present Value Concept

Present Value (PV) is the current value of a future sum of money or stream of cash flows given a specified rate of return. Formula: PV = FV ÷ (1 + r)ⁿ.

Effect of Compounding Frequency

As the frequency of compounding increases (from annual to semi-annual to monthly), the present value of a fixed future sum decreases because the effective interest rate per year increases.

Compound Interest Formula

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100n)ⁿt, where n is the number of times interest is compounded per year and t is the number of years.
